findings.title: $__range queries are interpolated before the no-split check
findings.body: runSplitQuery now runs datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target before querySupportsSplitting. That helper refuses to split expressions that still contain $__range, because the variable must be interpolated against each split window (the comment on querySupportsSplitting says backend interpolation of the split range is required). Template replacement consumes $__range using request.scopedVars for the full original range, so the check then sees a plain duration and splits the query anyway. Each chunk is executed with the full-range duration already baked in, so range-variable queries return wrong series. The $__range check has to happen on the raw expression, and $__range must not be replaced until each sub-range is known.

findings.title: Shard splitting interpolates, then runSplitQuery interpolates again
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery maps every target through applyTemplateVariables, then splitQueriesByStreamShard always delegates execution to runSplitQuery, which applies applyTemplateVariables a second time (the updated test even expects 5 calls for a single target). applyTemplateVariables also appends request.filters as ad-hoc matchers. The second pass therefore duplicates those matchers on an already rewritten expr, producing invalid or overly constrained LogQL and wrong results whenever ad-hoc filters are set. Interpolation for the shard path should happen once, and the inner runSplitQuery call must not template-replace targets that are already interpolated.

findings.title: Empty-after-interpolation queries are no longer dropped
findings.body: Previously interpolateVariablesInQueries ran before the expr/hide filters, so a target whose expression was only a variable that resolved to "" was removed and never queried. The new code filters on the raw expr first and only then calls applyTemplateVariables. A target like expr: "$query" that interpolates to an empty string now stays in the shard groups and is sent to Loki, which errors or returns unintended results. Filter again after interpolation, the same way the old interpolate-then-filter order did.
